Article Title: The towel on the chair: How it became India's ultimate status symbol
Article Text:
In India, a towel draped over an office chair often became a symbol of power, associated with a govt job.

Corruption = Monopoly + discretion - accountability

Abhishek Asthana is a tech & media entrepreneur. He runs a creative agency called GingerMonkey & is also the Co-founder of

Knot Dating

, a VC funded matrimony startup.

Long ago, my father told me a story about a certain ‘ Sunil ji. Nobody ever addressed him by his first name, it was always succeeded by a ‘ji’, because his office chair was covered with a towel.He would often wear a safari suit & a stiff-upper lip at family weddings. The guy with a govt job, an Afsar (officer), top billing in the arranged marriage market, despite having the lowest basic pay. At one such wedding, his wife blurted out an issue they were facing. Due to some clerical mistake, the details of their salary account was not updated, and Sunil ji wasn’t receiving his salary for over 2 years. They found this anomaly just last month. My family was grudgingly impressed, and hoped one of their kids turned out to be a towel-chair guy like Sunil ji.For much of modern India’s history, there wasn't enough. Jobs. College seats. Telephones. Gas cylinders. Batsmen with a good strike rate. We were short of everything. As if our nation came out of British rule like some of the TV reporters came out of the NEET protest, Gasping for breath, barely surviving the violence with almost all of the valuables stolen, but their morality, virtue and the associated pride intact.This was India in 1947.Such was the muscle memory of the rule, that we kept presenting our Annual budget at 5 PM IST, so that our British overlords could tune-in after having their breakfast. This tradition continued till 1999, more than 50 years after independence, until the Finance minister Yashwant Sinha , changed it to 11 AM. Imagine. The trauma of British rule never went away, it showed up in our metabolic wiring, in our insulin resistance, in our early onset of diabetes. Primarily due to the British administered famines. The bodies of our ancestors rewired to store fat. When the Brits eventually went back, they left behind quite a few problematic things like bureaucracy, Pakistan & monumental scarcity.When our leaders took over, they knew our demand vastly exceeded the supply, so they had to control the access of resources. And who do you trust to do that?Another British inheritance - The Collectorate. A regiment of people specifically trained to extract from the population, to collect revenues and give it back to the overlords, for whom serving people was optional, a hobby. A lot of them were corrupt too, In contrast there was barely any corruption among British officers, because they were paid almost 70 times the Indian officers. Hence, the Indians had to compensate with corruption. As we know, they continued compensating beyond independence as well. This coterie was assigned to allocate resources to Indians.No wonder, they acquired tremendous power. People began paying to jump the queue. When the government decided who could manufacture, import or expand a factory, permissions themselves became valuable commodities. British raj was eventually succeeded by Inspector Raj. And the underpaid inspectors lived in the same bungalows the British lived in.Economist Robert Klitgaard famously summarized it as:Whenever one person has monopoly over a decision, wide discretion, and little accountability, corruption happens.Accountability was like Vitamin-D for the country. We were always deficient. Add to that a lethargic judiciary. Some even justified corruption saying it's an essential lubricant for files to move without friction. A tool to facilitate ease of doing business. Many of the Indian billionaires today, exist due to their ancestors greasing their file-folders with this lubricant generously.Corruption is a chronic illness, it has been embedded in the DNA of a drought-coded, resource starved nation like ours. A government comes to power riding a wave of public anger. The previous regime is portrayed as irredeemably corrupt. Files are opened. Committees are formed. Raids happen. People are content. Finally, someone is cleaning the system.For a while, it genuinely feels different. Time passes, Power stops feeling temporary. The government begins winning elections. The public approval remains high. Loyalists become more confident. Criticism starts sounding less like feedback and more like conspiracy. Every institution gradually fills up with people who think alike.Corruption creeps up again. Like a virus - a parasite that needs a host - like a mosquito or a bat or a pigeon.Parasites don't advertise themselves. They attach themselves to something stronger. In India's case, this host is often identity - caste, religion, language. Every political movement needs an emotional engine. That engine mobilises voters, creates loyalty and builds political capital. Most of the time these issues are legitimate and deeply important. But once emotions become intense enough, they also become excellent camouflage. People stop asking uncomfortable questions because larger battles appear to be underway.If my religion is under threat, why discuss the waterlogged street near my house?If my caste is finally receiving justice, why focus on procurement irregularities?Not saying, Identity is not important. But we often forget to see what’s lurking behind it. The virus keeps growing, and one day it becomes bigger than the host, voters can see it, and it gets overthrown. Exit pollsters get shamed. The power of democracy is lauded. Until a new host emerges. The cycle continues. Elections just change the wrapper of the age-old system.Corruption will go away when we make it high-risk and low-reward. High salaries & high conviction rate. A Singaporean minister earns more than a top investment banker. And their corruption watchdog has a conviction rate of 99%. Our ED has at ~1%. This is the crux, until we fix it - another Sunil ji will discover they have a salary account a decade later.
Article Summary: In india, a towel draped over an office chair often became a symbol of power, associated with a govt job. Corruption = monopoly + discretion - accountability. Abhishek asthana is a tech & media entrepreneur. A tool to facilitate ease of doing business.

Article Title: Ramlila body asks 'Ramayana' makers to hold special screening before release, warns of protests
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Shri Ramlila Mahasangh has asked the makers of Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana to hold a special preview screening for its representatives before the film's worldwide theatrical release, warning that it will stage protests if the request is not accepted.In a letter addressed to director Nitesh Tiwari and the film's production company, Shri Ramlila Mahasangh president Arjun Kumar sought a screening of the film ahead of its Diwali 2026 release in India and overseas to ensure it does not contain scenes that could hurt Hindu sentiments.The demand comes in the backdrop of the controversy surrounding the 2023 film Adipurush, which drew criticism over its depiction of characters and settings from the Hindu epic.Recalling the earlier controversy, Kumar said members of the Sanatan community and those associated with traditional Ramlila performances had objected to several aspects of Adipurush, including "the depiction of Lanka in black instead of gold, and the portrayal of Ravana and his army in a manner that did not align with traditional beliefs.""According to information received by the Mahasangh, Ramayana may also contain certain scenes that could hurt the sentiments of Hindus living in India and abroad.In light of this, the organisation has requested a special preview screening to ensure that any potentially objectionable scenes or dialogues are identified and removed prior to release," Kumar said in a press note.He also warned that if the filmmakers do not agree to the request, the Shri Ramlila Mahasangh, along with various Hindu organisations, will stage protests and demonstrations outside cinema halls in Delhi and other states.The trailer of Ramayana was released during Brahma Muhurat and opens with Yash as Ravana emerging from the shadows before entering his palace and declaring his rule over the three worlds. It then introduces Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, with Arun Govil portraying King Dasharatha.The trailer also features Sai Pallavi as Sita, Ravie Dubey as Lakshmana, Rakul Preet Singh as Shurpanakha and key moments from the epic, including Rama and Sita's wedding, Sita's abduction and the build-up to the battle between Rama and Ravana. Sunny Deol plays Hanuman.The film's music has been composed by Hans Zimmer and AR Rahman. Ramayana: Part 1 is scheduled for a theatrical release during Diwali 2026, while Ramayana: Part 2 is slated to release during Diwali 2027.
Article Summary: The shri ramlila mahasangh has asked the makers of ranbir kapoor-starrer ramayana to hold a special preview screening. The demand comes in the backdrop of the controversy surrounding the 2023 film adipurush, which drew criticism over its depiction of characters and settings from the hindu epic.

Article Title: 'Disappointed with PM Modi': Shehzad Poonawalla’s sarcastic 'dictator' jibe at oppn after quitting BJP

NEW DELHI: A day after resigning from the party, former BJP national spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla on Saturday released an Instagram video saying he was “disappointed” with Prime Minister Narendra Modi In a sarcastic jibe at the Congress and its most prominent face, leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi , Poonawalla said that unlike Congress prime ministers, PM Modi, despite being in office for 12 years, was still to become a “dictator."Poonawalla’s remarks came after PM Modi, in his fifth Instagram video since the recent student protests in Delhi, said he had “forgiven” protesters who allegedly abused him and his late mother during the agitation. Several people, mostly youngsters, were booked for allegedly abusing the PM and his mother, after the protests ended with the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister on July 25.“I am completely disappointed with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. It has been 12 years and he has still not learnt how to be a dictator,” Poonawalla said in his Hindi video, adding that instead of becoming a dictator, the prime minister appealed for those who abused him to be forgiven.He urged the prime minister to learn “real dictatorship” from former prime ministers Indira Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru, Rahul Gandhi’s grandmother and great-grandfather, respectively. Poonawalla, a former Congress member, also referred to cases filed against students in Congress-ruled Karnataka and Kerala.He further referred to the alleged curbing of free speech during Nehru’s tenure and invoked the Emergency imposed by Indira Gandhi in 1975.“Who got all parliamentarians put in jail? Indira Gandhi. Who ordered police to fire at seers? Indira Gandhi,” Poonawalla remarked.The second incident he referred to appeared to be a reference to the 1966 police firing on protesters outside Parliament during a demonstration demanding a nationwide ban on cow slaughter.The former BJP spokesperson also referred to several protest movements that he alleged were “crushed” by Congress governments at the Centre and in various states.“We saw during the 2011 Anna Hazare agitation that 1,200-1,300 people were arrested. Anna Hazare himself was arrested. Rajbala lost her life,” he remarked, referring to the anti-corruption movement led by activist Anna Hazare that had put the then Congress-led UPA government under pressure.Rajbala was a woman protester who died following a Delhi Police crackdown at Ramlila Ground during the agitation.“Come on, Modi ji. It has been 12 years and you have still not become a dictator. You have poured water on the hopes of the Left-liberals,” Poonawalla concluded.PM Modi’s Instagram videos have been described as an attempt by the prime minister to reach out to “Gen Z” — the demographic with the largest participation in the recent student protests.
Article Summary: Former bjp national spokesperson shehzad poonawalla says he is 'disappointed' with pm narendra modi. He says pm modi, despite being in office for 12 years, was still to become a 'dictator' his remarks came after pm modi said he had 'forgiven' protesters who abused him and his mother.

Article Title: '2024 movement fooled Bangladesh': Taslima Nasreen's 'lesson' warning over Delhi student protests
Article Text:
Taslima Nasreen draws parallel between Bangladesh and Delhi student protest

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Sunday said the student movement that led to the ouster of Sheikh Hasina ’s government had “fooled us”, drawing a parallel between the protests in Bangladesh and the recent student demonstrations in Delhi.Speaking to reporters in Kolkata two days after returning to the city for the first time since 2007, the acclaimed writer acknowledged that she had not followed the Delhi protest closely, but added that a short video clip from the agitation “reminded me of the July 2024 students’ movement in Bangladesh.”"That student movement in Bangladesh fooled us. Because we thought the students wanted to abolish the quota system. Sheikh Hasina had also agreed to their demands, but ultimately the government fell. Later, we found that jihadis (Islamic fundamentalists) were behind that movement. The fallout has not been good for Bangladesh. Jihadis have taken over power there," she told reporters.Nasreen, who left Bangladesh in 1994 following threats from Islamic radicals over her work, further stated that the developments in her home country had “reinforced” her concerns about the consequences of such movements.The 63-year-old author added that the 2024 Bangladesh protests should “therefore serve as a lesson.”Nasreen’s remarks came ahead of the second anniversary of Sheikh Hasina’s resignation on August 5. The former prime minister has been living in exile in New Delhi.The Awami League government was replaced by an interim administration led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus three days after Sheikh Hasina’s ouster.In February this year, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) secured a sweeping victory in a landmark parliamentary election, paving the way for party chairperson Tarique Rahman to become the new prime minister.The protests in Delhi were held demanding the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET (UG) paper leak issue and seeking broader examination reforms. After more than five weeks of an indefinite sit-in led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in the national capital, Pradhan resigned on July 25, bringing the agitation to an end.
Article Summary: Taslima nasreen draws parallel between bangladesh and delhi student protest. Exiled bangladeshi author said the student movement that led to the ouster of sheikh hasina ’s government had ‘fooled us’

Article Title: ‘Ban on Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League a move against democracy’: Taslima Nasreen
Article Text:
Sheikh Hasina; Taslima Nasreen

Nasreen backs Uniform Civil Code , calls it necessary for women's equality

(With ANI inputs)

NEW DELHI: Exiled Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasreen on Sunday criticised the ban on former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League party, calling it a "move against democracy” and expressing uncertainty over Hasina’s return to the country.“No political party should be banned. The manner in which Sheikh Hasina was forced to leave the country is questionable. It was not right to ban the Awami League. It was a move against democracy. I want the ban to be lifted as soon as possible,” Nasreen told reporters at a press conference in Kolkata.Sheikh Hasina has been living in Delhi since August 5, 2024, after resigning as prime minister following weeks of student-led protests. The interim government led by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus, which took charge after the fall of the Awami League administration, banned the party in May 2025 under anti-terrorism laws.Meanwhile, Nasreen alleged that several Awami League workers had been tortured and killed during Sheikh Hasina’s exile and expressed uncertainty over whether the former prime minister would be able to return to Bangladesh.“Many Awami League workers were tortured and murdered. Sheikh Hasina wants to return, but I do not know whether that will be possible.But no one wants me to go back,” she said.Nasreen also criticised Jamaat-e-Islami, now Bangladesh's principal opposition party, accusing it of opposing women’s equality and seeking the imposition of Sharia law.“Now we have Jamaat-e-Islami as an opposition party. It is against women’s equality, and they want Sharia rule. If that happens, no minority will survive. Bangladesh is moving towards darkness. No one is trying to civilise Bangladesh. The government is only trying to remain in power,” she added.The 63-year-old author further claimed that “hatred against Hindus” was being spread in some madrasas and mosques in Bangladesh.“In many madrasas and mosques, hatred is being taught against Hindus,” Nasreen remarked.Turning to the issue of the Uniform Civil Code (UCC), Nasreen said she had been advocating for such a law for the past 40 years and described it as essential in any “civilised country”.“I have been fighting for the UCC for the past 40 years. This is much needed in any civilised country,” she remarked.She claimed that religious laws continued to affect women’s rights in Bangladesh, alleging that Hindu women in the country lacked adequate legal protections, including the right to divorce.“In Bangladesh, Hindu girls have no rights; they do not even have the right to divorce. Due to religious laws, women are suffering. Hindus are being tortured in Bangladesh. During the Yunus regime, Hindus were tortured even more,” she alleged.In July, the BJP-led West Bengal government constituted a nine-member expert committee headed by retired Supreme Court judge Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai to examine and finalise a draft UCC for the state. The state government plans to introduce the legislation during the upcoming August Assembly session.Nasreen, who has lived in exile since 1994, when she was forced to leave Bangladesh due to the threat from Islamic radicals over her work, returned to Kolkata nearly two decades. She was forced to leave the city in 2007 following protests over her writings and memoir Dwikhandito (Split into Two), published in 2003.
Article Summary: Sheikh hasina has been living in delhi since august 5, 2024, after resigning as prime minister following weeks of student-led protests. The interim government led by nobel laureate muhammad yunus, which took charge after the fall of the awami league administration, banned the party in may 2025 under anti-terrorism laws.

Article Title: Indian diaspora in China flags anti-India social media posts, visa curbs at 1st embassy outreach
Article Text:
The outreach comes as India and China continue efforts to improve bilateral ties after years of strained relations

NEW DELHI: Members of the Indian diaspora in China raised concerns over anti-India content on Chinese social media, declining work visas and employment restrictions for spouses during an Open House hosted by the Indian Embassy in Beijing.The outreach event, held on Friday, had Indian Ambassador Vikram Doraiswami and senior embassy officials interact with professionals from across sectors on issues affecting the Indian community in China.Participants flagged what they described as a growing trend of abusive posts targeting Indians, including comments on Indian culture and food habits, besides raising concerns over the declining number of work visas being issued by Chinese authorities and difficulties faced by spouses seeking employment, reported PTI.Addressing the gathering, Doraiswami said Chinese authorities were aware of the increase in such online content and were taking measures to curb it. He added that the embassy was responding by pushing verified, fact-based information through its official social media channels.The ambassador also announced that documentation requirements for Chinese citizens applying for Indian visas would be eased from next week to encourage greater travel to India.Seeking to improve support for the Indian community, the embassy is working on a legal assistance framework for professionals facing workplace-related issues in China and plans to institutionalise the Open House as a regular forum for addressing consular and community concerns.Doraiswami also said the mission would expand cultural outreach programmes, including events such as the Vasant Mela, to promote India's cultural diversity and cuisine.The interaction comes amid efforts by New Delhi and Beijing to stabilise bilateral relations, with Doraiswami, who assumed charge in May, stepping up diplomatic engagement with Chinese officials.

Article Title: 'Dismantle terror infrastructure first': India's US envoy hits out at Pakistan over Indus Waters Treaty
Article Text:

India’s envoy to the US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra said Pakistan had eroded the foundation of the Indus Waters Treaty over the past five decades. He added that Islamabad had “dismantled” the goodwill and friendship that underpinned the 1960 agreement, and that New Delhi’s decision to keep the treaty in abeyance merely acknowledged that reality.As reported by US' Newsweek magazine, Kwatra said the treaty’s preamble reflected a commitment made 'in a spirit of goodwill and friendship', but Pakistan’s conduct had weakened that foundation over half a century.“It is worth remembering that the treaty's preamble declares it was concluded ‘in a spirit of goodwill and friendship’. Pakistan spent half a century dismantling that goodwill and friendship. The abeyance merely acknowledges what Pakistan's conduct had already destroyed,” Kwatra said.His remarks came after Pakistan recently hosted a conference protesting India’s decision to keep the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance on April 23 last year, a day after Pakistan-trained terrorists killed 26 people in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir.The IWT, signed by India and Pakistan in 1960, divided the waters of the six rivers of the Indus basin between the two countries. India was given control over the eastern rivers, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej which account for about 20 per cent of the basin’s water, while Pakistan received rights over the western rivers Indus, Jhelum and Chenab carrying around 80 per cent.“That asymmetry stifled development for decades in Indian regions that could have benefited from better water rights. India honoured the treaty anyway,” Kwatra said according to Newsweek.The envoy said Pakistan’s approach towards India had been marked by wars, hostility and cross-border terrorism, citing the 1965, 1971 and 1999 conflicts along with major terror attacks, including the 2001 Parliament attack, the 2008 Mumbai attacks, the 2016 Uri and Pathankot attacks, the 2019 Pulwama attack and the 2025 Pahalgam attack.Kwatra also said that if Pakistan sincerely wanted India’s cooperation on bilateral issues, it must first dismantle the terror infrastructure it has built over the years.On implementation of the treaty, Kwatra alleged that Pakistan had repeatedly delayed Indian projects and opposed efforts to revisit the agreement in view of changing technology and requirements.“Pakistan also consistently blocked India's initiatives to renegotiate the treaty in light of six decades of technological change, which would have let India develop its hydropower potential,” Kwatra added.“Bit by bit, Pakistan eroded India's faith that it could exercise its rights under the treaty, or hope for a better one suited to today's realities,” he said.Responding to calls for India and Pakistan to resume talks, Kwatra said past initiatives had failed to address core concerns.“Prime Minister Narendra Modi has clearly voiced India’s stand today: ‘Terror and talks cannot go together... Terror and trade cannot go together... Water and blood cannot flow together',” Kwatra said.Kwatra also said Pakistan should focus on improving its own water management instead of blaming India for its challenges."The Government of Pakistan would do better to fix its dismal water productivity, than to stage conferences blaming India and issuing threats,” he said, adding, “The habit of pinning every domestic failure on India has grown old."
Article Summary: India’s envoy to the us, vinay mohan kwatra said pakistan had eroded the foundation of the indus waters treaty over the past five decades. He added that islamabad had “dismantled” the goodwill and friendship that underpinned the 1960 agreement. The iwt, signed by india and pakistan in 1960, divided the waters of the six rivers of theindus basin between the countries.

Article Title: Judge Ujjal Bhuyan questions SC collegium’s opacity
Article Text:
Citizens have right to know deliberations on elevation, transfer of judges: Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: SC judge Ujjal Bhuyan has questioned opacity in the collegium’s decisions on judicial appointments.“I have noticed that the last three collegium resolutions contain no reasons whatsoever. Is this a step back from the principle of transparency?” said Justice Bhuyan at a panel discussion on Saturday. “By withholding reasons, we also create space for individuals to enter the judiciary who may later describe groups of people as ‘ants’ and make other remarks that are wholly unconstitutional,” he said.To prevent the entry of such people, “there should be some discussion, there should be some reasons given”, said Justice Ujjal Bhuyan. Though the judge didn’t name anyone, the comment was an apparent reference to a remark by an Allahabad high court judge at a social event in 2024.He was speaking at the launch of the Judicial Transparency Index: Assessing Disclosure of Information by the Supreme Court and the High Courts, prepared by the Justice, Access and Lowering Delays in India (JALDI) Initiative at the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy.The judge stressed that deliberations on the elevation and transfer of judges by the SC collegium largely remain confidential, contrary to the principle of judicial transparency.“While carrying out the next assessment on the scale of Judicial Transparency Index, I may request the JALDI team to also look into the aspect of opacity of the collegium system. Deliberations on elevation and transfer of judges remain confidential. Reasons for rejecting or deferring a recommendation are rarely disclosed in full. And the criteria applied are not codified in any publicly disclosed instrument. It is a very important issue. Citizens have a right to know what is happening in the courts. They have a right to know who would be their judges.They have a right to know judgments. These should be in the public domain”, Justice Bhuyan underlined.The report is the first systematic study assessing transparency practices across India’s higher judiciary and evaluates disclosure of information by the Supreme Court and high courts across judicial processes, institutional governance and administration, and judicial and administrative personnel.Referring to a previous collegium resolution reiterating the recommendation of senior advocate Saurabh Kirpal for appointment as a judge, Justice Bhuyan said he found the reasons recorded by the Supreme Court convincing but noted that despite more than three and a half years having passed, no appointment materialised.Key findings of the JALDI report reveal that only five high courts have published a budget on their websites for FY 2025-26 while none has published the criteria governing case allocation.Of the 813 judges in the higher judiciary, only 87 have publicly disclosed their assets even as only two high courts publish disciplinary sanction orders pertaining to district judicial officers.“The findings highlight that the level of judicial transparency varies across courts and demonstrate that while individual disclosure measures have emerged...they have not yet translated into a holistic approach...” a release from Vidhi said.
Article Summary: Citizens have right to know deliberations on elevation, transfer of judges: bhuyan. Only five high courts have published a budget on their websites for fy 2025-26 while none has published the criteria governing case allocation. Of the 813 judges in the higher judiciary, only 87 have publicly disclosed their assets.

Article Title: RBI updates deposit rules: From differential rates to daily disclosures, here's what's changing
Article Text:
RBI changes deposit rules, allows differential bulk deposit rates and tighter disclosures.

Differential rates on bulk deposits

Mandatory daily disclosure of bulk deposit rates



Uniform rates for similarly placed depositors to continue

NEW DELHI: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has overhauled rules governing bulk deposits, allowing banks to offer differential interest rates based on liquidity risk under the Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) framework while mandating daily public disclosure of bulk deposit rates to improve transparency.The revised instructions amend the Reserve Bank of India (Interest Rate on Deposits) Directions, 2025, and will come into force from October 1, 2026.The RBI has allowed banks to offer different interest rates on bulk deposits after factoring in the liquidity risk associated with such deposits under the LCR framework."A bank shall have the freedom to offer differential interest rate on bulk deposits, by considering the differential run-off rate applicable to deposits or unsecured wholesale funding under the LCR framework," the RBI said, as quoted by ANI.The provision applies to both domestic rupee deposits and rupee deposits held by non-residents. According to the central bank, the move aligns deposit pricing with the revised LCR framework outlined in the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Asset Liability Management) Directions, 2025.In a move aimed at improving transparency, the RBI has directed banks to publish bulk deposit interest rates on their websites every business day.Under the revised rules, banks must disclose the applicable rates by 10:00 am, with a grace period of up to 10:10 am."Interest rates payable on deposits, including bulk deposits, shall be strictly as per the schedule of interest rates disclosed in advance on the bank's website," the RBI said.The daily disclosure requirement is intended to make bulk deposit pricing more transparent and ensure customers have access to the latest rates.While giving banks greater flexibility in pricing bulk deposits, the RBI has retained the principle that similarly placed depositors must be treated equally."The interest rates offered on deposits, including bulk deposits, shall be uniform across all branches and for all customers and there shall be no discrimination... between one deposit and another deposit of similar amount, accepted on the same date, at any of its offices," the RBI said.This means banks cannot offer different rates to customers with similar deposits solely based on location or individual negotiations if the deposits are otherwise identical.
Article Summary: Rbi changes deposit rules, allows differential bulk deposit rates and tighter disclosures. Differential rates on bulk deposits can be based on liquidity risk under the liquidity coverage ratio (lcr) framework. The daily disclosure requirement is intended to make bulk deposit pricing more transparent.

Donovan Mitchell reportedly marries Coco Jones

The beautiful love story of Donovan Mitchell and Coco Jones

Donovan Mitchell and Coco Jones. Image via: John Nacion/ Getty Images

Fans congratulate Donovan Mitchell and Coco Jones

Donovan Mitchell has reportedly married singer and actress Coco Jones , marking a major personal milestone during the NBA offseason. Former basketball player Troy Payne shared videos from the ceremony on his Instagram Story, while Complex Sports also reported the wedding on Instagram. Neither Mitchell nor Jones has publicly confirmed the marriage, but the videos quickly drew attention from fans celebrating the couple's latest chapter.The reported wedding comes just over a year after the Cleveland Cavaliers star and the Grammy-winning artist announced their engagement. Their relationship has largely stayed out of the spotlight, making the emergence of wedding footage a rare glimpse into one of sports and music's most private power couples.While Mitchell and Jones have yet to share the news themselves, the videos posted by Payne offered fans their first look at what appeared to be the couple's wedding day. The report follows months of anticipation after the pair confirmed their engagement in July 2025. Representatives for the couple previously revealed they got engaged while on vacation after a busy stretch that included Mitchell's NBA season and Jones' sold-out tour.Jones has often spoken about the significance of their relationship. In an interview with PEOPLE earlier this year, she described marriage as more than just another milestone."I think about my life so much like business, and I'm like, 'Girl, you got to stop. This is the biggest contract I've ever signed.' You know what I'm saying? This is a real-life, forever commitment," she told PEOPLE. "I talk about forever, I sing about forever, and then I'm like, 'Oh, this really forever. Okay, word up, word up.' "She also explained why their relationship has been strong."We both go really hard for the things we love, and they're demanding careers," she said. "I feel like we speak a different language that makes me really feel seen. And he's my biggest cheerleader, so I feel like I'm never able to doubt myself in his presence. It's just not going down like that."Their relationship began in 2023 after meeting at a networking event for creatives where phones were not allowed. Jones later revealed the unusual setting helped them form a genuine connection, adding that Mitchell had actually tried reaching out years earlier after seeing her on Bel-Air, but she never noticed his Instagram message.Reflecting on that missed opportunity, Jones said, "He said he sent something with a red heart and that wouldn’t have worked for me anyways." She added, "That’s how you know it’s above us, it’s God. We’re meant to be."The couple announced their engagement in July 2025 with photos and video from the proposal. Russell Wilson and Ciara even played a role in helping organize the special moment, with Wilson writing, "Ciara and I are so happy for you two. Thanks for allowing us to plan this with you."Despite growing public interest, both have consistently chosen privacy over publicity. "He has never been a secret," Jones explained. "I am not trying to hide him or hide us. I feel like I give a lot to the world and it's mine." She added that keeping parts of their relationship private allows it to be authentic.Mitchell has been equally open about what Jones means to him, saying during Cavaliers media day, "Man, that's my dog. I love her to death. She's amazing. She's an amazing human being. She brings me peace." He later added, "She's a special human... and to be able to call her my fiancée, my wife, is a blessing. So, I'm grateful."The reported wedding sparked an outpouring of congratulatory messages across social media. Among the standout reactions were:One fan wrote, "Congrats y'all!"Another shared, "Congratulations"One fan wishes the couple: "Congrats and God Bless! 🙌❤️"Another user wrote: "Love this for her ❤️"One shared: "BLACK LOVEEEEE💍"Another commented: "Spidaman & Spidawoman 🔥👏🏾"The responses reflected the admiration many fans have shown for Mitchell and Jones throughout their relationship. As the couple continues to balance successful careers in basketball and music, the reported wedding marks another memorable milestone in a love story that has largely unfolded on their own terms.
Article Summary: Donovan mitchell reportedly married singer and actress coco jones. Former basketball player troy payne shared videos from the ceremony on his instagram story. Neither mitchell nor jones has publicly confirmed the marriage. The reported wedding sparked an outpouring of congratulatory messages across social media.

Article Title: Trump 'cancels' Iran strikes as rapid deal aims to reopen Hormuz, curb nuclear threat
Article Text:
Trump says US is 'locked and loaded at levels of military readiness not seen since WWII' despite calling off strikes

US President Donald Trump on Sunday claimed that the United States had been "locked and loaded" with military force against Iran at levels "not seen since World War II" but said he decided to call off the planned attack after Tehran and several Middle Eastern countries urged to hold off and pushed to make a deal.In a post on Truth Social, Trump said Iran had requested that Washington "hold off any attack" after the broad parameters of an agreement had been reached. "The USA is locked and loaded and ready to go against the Islamic Republic of Iran, at levels of Military Terror, Strength, and Power not seen since World War II," Trump wrote.Despite the military preparations, Trump said he had agreed to cancel the attack after being approached by Iran and other regional countries."Based on this request, I have agreed... to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL," he added.According to Trump, the proposed agreement would include the "immediate, complete, and total" reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and "an end to Iran's nuclear threat."He also claimed that Israel had backed the decision. "The Country of Israel joins me in this commitment," Trump said, urging all parties to finalise the agreement."Get to work, everybody, and get it DONE," he added.Iranian authorities had not immediately commented on Trump's claims.This came after reports swirled that the US and Israel were planning a potential bombing campaign targeting Iran's energy infrastructure, with strikes possibly taking place over the weekend. According to CBS News, citing multiple US sources, officials discussed wrapping up the operation before financial markets open on Monday amid concerns over the potential impact of the strikes on the US and global economy.
Article Summary: Trump says us is 'locked and loaded at levels of military readiness not seen since wwii' despite calling off strikes. Trump says iran had requested that washington "hold off any attack" after the broad parameters of an agreement had been reached. Reports swirled that the us and israel were planning a potential bombing campaign targeting iran's energy infrastructure.

Article Title: 'Enjoys playing victim card': Congress attacks PM Modi's 'forgive youth' remark
Article Text:
Jairam Ramesh accuses PM Modi of playing 'victim card'

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe PM Modi should apologize for the issues raised by Jairam Ramesh? Yes, he should apologize No, he shouldn't apologize 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Saturday criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his remarks about "forgiving" the country's youth.He said the Prime Minister should instead apologise over a range of issues, including alleged exam paper leaks, the treatment of student protesters, demonetisation and the functioning of the Ram Mandir Trust.In a post on X, Ramesh said, "The self-declared non-biological PM enjoys playing the victim card." He further alleged that the Prime Minister "uses vile vitriol against his predecessors and political opponents" and "very frequently peddles lies to defame them, not just in his public speeches but in Parliament itself.""He uses vile vitriol against his predecessors and political opponents. He very frequently peddles lies to defame them, not just in his public speeches but in Parliament itself. He unleashes an army of foul-mouthed abusers both in Parliament and outside and gives them full protection," Ramesh said.Referring to the National Testing Agency (NTA) and student protests, Ramesh said, "the entire nation is wanting the PM to apologise for the trauma inflicted on lakhs of youth through his paper leak-ridden NTA and his Home Ministry-sanctioned brutality on student protestors."He also said the Prime Minister owed an apology over the "Chanda Chori Astha Dhoka by the Ram Mandir Trust" and for the "Tughlakian notebandi of Nov 8 2016 that destroyed crores of livelihoods and shuttered lakhs if MSMEs."Ramesh added, "but late last night, in act of supreme self-obsession, the PM said that he forgave our youth." He alleged that the remark was "an insult to the nation and to our youth", adding that young people had suffered under the government's policies and were instead seeking an apology from the Prime Minister."The Prime Minister’s InstaGram Sabhas are fooling no one," Ramesh added.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday shared a video late at night that carried a message against abusive language and hate, saying "abuses never solve anything," amid a controversy over alleged derogatory remarks made against him by a woman from Noida during a protest in Delhi."Abuses never solve anything. Let’s guide the misguided. Let’s work together. Let’s work for Bharat," PM Modi wrote, sharing the video on X.In the video, PM Modi also highlighted the government's efforts to strengthen the country's examination system, citing Parliament's passage of a stringent anti-paper leak law."Friends, we are continuously taking one step after another to build a trustworthy examination system. Whether it is creating fast-track mechanisms or incorporating suggestions from the states, we are working in that direction."The Prime Minister said paper leaks had affected governments across the country for decades and jeopardised the future of students.PM Modi reiterated that the government would act firmly against those involved in paper leak rackets.
Article Summary: Jairam ramesh accuses pm modi of playing 'victim card' with remarks about 'forgiving' the country's youth. He said pm should instead apologise over a range of issues, including alleged exam paper leaks, the treatment of student protesters, demonetisation and the functioning of the ram mandir trust.

Article Title: 'In every national security decision, Doval had a role': Amit Shah praises NSA at award ceremony
Article Text:
Amit Shah presented Lokmanya Tilak award to Ajit Doval and hailed his role in India's national security

'First selection' after Modi became PM

Shah invokes Lokmanya Tilak's legacy

'Award will inspire those who serve the nation'

Doval accepts award with humility

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday lauded National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval for his contribution to India's national security and foreign policy, saying the veteran intelligence officer has played a crucial role behind every major national security decision taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014.Speaking at a function in Pune after presenting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award 2026 to Doval, Shah said the NSA's advice and strategic inputs have been instrumental in strengthening India's security architecture and defence preparedness.He also said Doval's contribution to India's internal and external security had been so significant that history would reserve "a golden page" for him."NSA Ajit Doval has played a great role in strengthening India's foreign policy. In every decision of PM Modi for national security, Doval has had a 'role and advice' in the background," Shah said."Whenever history is written, if anyone analyses internal security and external security, then clearly, for Ajit Doval ji, a golden page will have to be kept reserved; there is no doubt about this," he added.Shah said one of the first decisions taken by PM Modi after assuming office in 2014 was appointing Doval as the National Security Advisor, a move he said transformed India's strategic posture."Today, India's foreign policy has become a foreign policy with a backbone of steel; no one can deny this. We have, along with self-respect, strengthened our position in the world," Shah said.Praising Doval's decades-long career in the Intelligence Bureau, Shah said India has emerged as a stronger and more confident nation under Modi's leadership, with Doval making a significant contribution to that transformation."After becoming NSA in 2014, Doval helped implement many strategic ideas on the ground and played a major role in modernising India's armed forces, strengthening technology, enhancing operational capability and improving the country's defence preparedness," Shah said.He added that the Modi government has fundamentally transformed both the defensive and offensive capabilities of the armed forces over the past 12 years, with Doval playing a key role in the process.Shah also noted that much of Doval's contribution can never be made public because of the confidential nature of intelligence operations.Recalling his tenure as Gujarat's home minister, Shah narrated how he first interacted with Doval following the Ahmedabad serial bomb blasts. He said then chief minister Narendra Modi had advised Gujarat Police to consult Doval while investigating the attacks."I remember Ajit ji had come to my house. The tips he gave resulted in Gujarat Police resolving not just the Ahmedabad bomb blast, but 13 bomb blasts across the country all at once. This was a very great achievement," Shah said.The Union home minister also paid tribute to Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, calling him one of the foremost architects of India's freedom movement.He said Tilak's iconic slogan, "Swarajya is my birthright, and I shall have it," gave a new direction to India's freedom struggle and inspired generations of freedom fighters.Shah added that the slogan made Indians realise that self-rule was their right and not a favour bestowed by anyone.Describing Tilak as a fearless journalist, Shah said one could truly understand courage in journalism only by reading the articles published in Kesari, the newspaper founded by the freedom fighter."How fearless a journalist can be can only be experienced by reading the articles of Kesari," he said.Referring to Tilak's role in mobilising people through the public Ganesh and Shivaji festivals, Shah said they laid the foundation for cultural nationalism and that India continues to follow the path envisioned by the freedom fighter."India is now moving firmly on the path of cultural nationalism laid down by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and no one can reverse that journey," he said.Shah further added that Tilak's ideas on nationalism, self-rule and social awakening continue to guide the country and remain relevant for nation-building, particularly for the younger generation.Shah said honours such as the Lokmanya Tilak National Award are not merely ceremonial but recognise those who dedicate their lives to the country and inspire future generations."When such individuals are honoured, the feeling of gratitude of society towards them is discharged... Today, the Tilak Award that has been conferred upon Ajit Doval ji... for those who live for this country and work for this country, it will become a place of great inspiration," he said.Accepting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award, Doval thanked the organisers and said he was honoured to receive an award named after Lokmanya Tilak."I am thankful for this award named after Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and accept it with humility," Doval said.Doval also praised the country's leadership, saying, "We are very fortunate to have leaders like PM Modi and Amit Shah".
Article Summary: Amit shah presented lokmanya tilak award to ajit doval and hailed his role in india's national security. Shah said the nsa's advice and strategic inputs have been instrumental in strengthening india's security architecture and defence preparedness.

Article Title: US makes $20,000 visa bond programme permanent; India not on 50-country list
Article Text:
India not on list

Who will be affected?

The US State Department has decided to make its visa bond programme permanent after successfully running it as a pilot scheme, expanding a policy aimed at reducing visa overstays. The programme currently applies to citizens of 50 countries.Under the new rule, consular officers may require certain applicants for US visitor visas to post a bond of up to $20,000 before a visa is issued. The regulation takes effect on August 3, when it is scheduled to be published in the Federal Register. US officials have indicated that additional countries could be added to the programme in the future, Reuters cites.The visa bond programme currently covers citizens of 50 countries, including Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan, but India is not among them. This means Indian applicants for B-1 (business) and B-2 (tourist) visas are not affected by the new rule at present.However, the State Department has indicated that more countries could be added to the programme in the future.The rule applies to applicants seeking B-1 (business) and B-2 (tourism) visas from countries covered under the programme.According to the Federal Register notice, "Consular officers may require covered nonimmigrant visa applicants to post a bond of up to $20,000 as a condition of visa issuance, as determined by the consular officers."The State Department said a year-long review of the pilot programme found that visa bonds were effective in encouraging travellers to comply with the terms of their stay in the United States.During the pilot programme launched in 2025, consular officers could require visa applicants to post bonds of $5,000, $10,000 or $15,000.Under the permanent rule, the $5,000 option has been removed and the maximum bond amount has been increased to $20,000.Immigration and rights advocates have criticised the policy, arguing that requiring applicants to deposit thousands of dollars could discourage legitimate travel to the United States.The visa bond programme is part of a broader immigration crackdown under President Donald Trump.
Article Summary: The us state department has decided to make its visa bond programme permanent. The policy is aimed at reducing visa overstays. It currently covers citizens of 50 countries, including bangladesh, nepal and bhutan. India is not on the list of countries covered by the programme.

Article Title: 'You are a fool to live so openly, Mallya told Nirav before his arrest'
Article Text:
TOI correspondent from London

: Economic fugitive Vijay Mallya invited fellow billionaire Nirav Modi to his multi-million-pound townhouse overlooking Regent's Park where the pair discussed their respective exiles when the latter was living freely in London before his arrest, the final podcast of the "Diamond King", released Friday, claims.A source in the diamond trade who tipped off Telegraph about Nirav's location, leading to his arrest in March 2019, claims in Episode 4: "Mallya and Nirav were in contact... "Mallya told him he was a fool for living so openly and told him he was too exposed, but Nirav didn't listen.""It's possible Mallya's blueprint gave Nirav the confidence he didn't need to hide." But Nirav did not get bail and has been in a London jail for seven years.Despite an Interpol red notice, Nirav "would regularly stop for a cup of coffee at a cafe in Oxford Street where he would sit reading newspapers... where anyone could see him," the source said. However, he started taking precautions later. To avoid being seen in restaurants, he would pay private chefs £200 to £300 per hour to come to his apartment and cook, but they were never of Indian origin, and it was never the same chef twice, the podcast revealed."I don't think he was clever enough to come up with the (Punjab National Bank) scam himself," the source added. The podcast speculates that Nirav has submitted a second asylum case, which is why he has not gone back. Nirav's solicitor Anand Doobay, who Mallya also used, told TOI: "We are not commenting."
Article Summary: Vijay mallya invited nirav modi to his multi-million-pound townhouse overlooking regent's park. The pair discussed their respective exiles when the latter was living freely in london. A source in the diamond trade who tipped off telegraph about nirav's location, leading to his arrest, claims in episode 4: "mallya and nirav were in contact"

Article Title: Spain says most migrants return to Morocco after border rush kills 57
Article Text:
As thousands gathered near the border, Moroccan security forces used batons and tear gas to push back crowds

Spain said on Friday that it had regained control of a massive migrant surge into its North African enclave of Ceuta, with most of the more than 50,000 people who crossed the border by land and sea voluntarily returning to Morocco. The unprecedented influx left dozens dead and triggered political tensions across Europe.Spanish authorities said 57 bodies had been recovered on the Spanish side of the border. Officials warned that the death toll could be higher as there may have been additional casualties on the Moroccan side. According to the government, some migrants drowned while others were crushed as they attempted to climb the breakwater supporting the border fence.Spain's interior ministry said around 50,000 migrants entered Ceuta between Thursday and Friday, with about 48,300 having already returned to Morocco by Friday evening. Ceuta regional president Juan Jesus Vivas, however, estimated that the total number of crossings could have reached 60,000 over the two days.As thousands gathered near the border, Moroccan security forces used batons and tear gas to push back crowds and prevent more people from entering the Spanish territory.Reuters reporters at the scene also saw riot police firing tear gas, while water cannon vehicles were deployed to disperse migrants. Burnt remains of a bus and seven cars were visible following clashes.On the Spanish side, military vehicles were positioned along sections of the border as hundreds of migrants remained stranded on the Moroccan side. Several hundred people later crossed back through official checkpoints and openings in the fence, with many saying they were unable to find food or shelter in Ceuta. "I'm going back," one migrant told news agency Reuters.Spanish prime minister Pedro Sanchez travelled to Ceuta on Friday, where he faced protests and jeers from demonstrators. He described the mass border crossing as "a violation of Spain's territorial sovereignty" and said authorities were accelerating the return of those who had entered illegally with Morocco's full cooperation.The incident also exposed divisions within Europe over migration policy. Italy announced it was temporarily suspending the European Union's Schengen border-free travel arrangements with Spain, a decision that would affect air and sea travel between the two countries. Madrid criticised the move, saying it breached European Union treaties.Ceuta and Melilla, Spain's two autonomous enclaves in North Africa, form the European Union's only land borders with Africa. While both regularly witness attempts by migrants to enter Europe, Spanish authorities described the latest influx as unprecedented.Several right-wing political parties across Europe blamed the crisis on Spain's migration policies, including this year's amnesty for hundreds of thousands of undocumented migrants. Spain also summoned the Italian ambassador after Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani claimed the amnesty had "encouraged human trafficking".US President Donald Trump also weighed in on the crisis, describing the situation at Ceuta as an invasion.The crossings "look like an invasion", Trump said, adding, "That same thing's going to happen to us if the Republicans don't get elected, except worse," referring to the upcoming US midterm elections.The US state department also criticised Spain's handling of migration, saying the incident was "the direct result of the Spanish Government's deliberate efforts to enable and facilitate mass illegal migration into Europe." It added, "We are considering actions to defend Americans at home and abroad from this threat and stand ready to assist other European allies considering similar option."Meanwhile, France said it would significantly strengthen security along its border with Spain.French interior minister Laurent Nunez announced that the police presence would be increased fivefold by Saturday, alongside enhanced aerial surveillance and additional patrols on trains.Spain's Guardia Civil police association AUGC also criticised the handling of the situation, saying there had been too few officers deployed at the border fence during the surge, leaving security forces unable to stop the mass crossings.
Article Summary: Spain says it has regained control of a massive migrant surge into its north african enclave of ceuta. Most of the more than 50,000 people who crossed the border by land and sea voluntarily returned to morocco. The unprecedented influx left dozens dead and triggered political tensions across europe.

Article Title: 4.7-magnitude earthquake hits Italy; buildings damaged, four injured
Article Text:
4.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Italy, injures four (Reuters image)

A 4.7-magnitude earthquake struck the volcanic Campi Flegrei (Phlegraean Fields) area near the southern Italian city of Naples on Friday, injuring four people, damaging buildings and churches. It also triggered power outages that disrupted train and metro services.The earthquake struck at 7.46 pm (local time), with its epicentre in the Campi Flegrei volcanic area west of Naples at a depth of about 3 km (2 miles), according to Italy's National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology.The Italian fire service said minor damage was reported to buildings in and around Naples, but added that emergency crews had not received any immediate requests for rescue or assistance, as cited by Reuters.As a precaution, local authorities suspended rail and metro services while inspections were carried out.Italian media described the tremor as one of the strongest ever recorded in the Campi Flegrei area, prompting residents in several neighbourhoods to rush onto the streets as the ground shook.Campi Flegrei, a densely populated volcanic caldera that spans much of western Naples, has witnessed increasingly frequent seismic activity in recent years, prompting Italian authorities to intensify monitoring of the area.While low-intensity tremors are common in the region, stronger earthquakes have revived concerns over a repeat of the seismic crisis of the early 1980s, which caused widespread disruption and forced thousands of residents to evacuate their homes.Italy is prone to earthquakes due to its geological setting. In 2016, a series of powerful quakes struck central Italy, devastating parts of the Lazio, Umbria and Marche regions and killing around 300 people.The country's deadliest earthquake in recent decades was the 6.9-magnitude Irpinia quake in southern Italy in November 1980, which claimed about 2,700 lives and devastated hundreds of towns.
Article Summary: 4.7-magnitude earthquake strikes italy, injures four people. It struck the volcanic campi flegrei (phlegraean fields) area near the southern italian city of naples. It also triggered power outages that disrupted train and metro services.

Article Title: US Marine F-35 fighter jet crashes in San Diego, pilot ejects safely
Article Text:
Military officials said the cause of the crash is being investigated.

A US Marine Corps F-35 fighter jet crashed near Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Miramar in San Diego on Friday, with the pilot ejecting safely before the aircraft burst into flames and sparked a brush fire, military officials said.The fighter aircraft, attached to the 3rd Marine Aircraft Wing and Marine Aircraft Group 11, went down at around 10 am local time near the air station. The Marine Corps described the incident as an "aircraft mishap".First Lieutenant Blake Starbuck told Fox News that the crash was a "Class A mishap involving a Marine Corps F-35B in the vicinity of MCAS Miramar".Lieutenant Starbuck confirmed that the pilot successfully ejected and was safely recovered after the aircraft came down. Military officials said the cause of the crash is being investigated.Starbuck said he could not immediately confirm the purpose of the flight, including whether the aircraft had been taking off, landing or carrying out a training mission.He also said there was no immediate information about any injuries or fatalities linked to the crash.Television footage from SkyRanger 7 showed the wreckage split into two large sections in the middle of a burnt field roughly the size of a football pitch.Large flames and thick black smoke rose from the crash site, which was located north of State Route 52, making the fire visible to motorists on the nearby highway. The San Diego Fire-Rescue Department said it had joined efforts to contain the brush fire triggered by the crash.However, officials said the military remains in charge of the crash site and will lead the investigation into the incident.
Article Summary: Us marine corps f-35 fighter jet crashed near marine corps air station (mcas) miramar in san diego. Pilot ejected safely before the aircraft burst into flames and sparked a brush fire. Military officials said the cause of the crash is being investigated.
